title: The Turkish Meze Board
seo_title: Turkish Meze Board: Sucuk, Pastırma & Dips for 8–10
description: A Turkish meze board with grilled sucuk, pastırma, beyaz peynir, kaşar, four dips, simit and warm pide. The full shopping list for 8–10 guests.
hook: A meyhane-style spread: warm sucuk and pide, a ring of dips and plenty of white cheese. Generous portions are the point.
why: Two cured beef meats set the tone. Sucuk is a garlicky, cumin-spiced sausage that crisps in a pan, and pastırma is air-dried beef in a fenugreek and pepper crust. Mild beef salami gives cautious guests somewhere to start, and brined beyaz peynir, with its clean saltiness, resets the palate between rich bites.

The dips do the balancing. Earthy hummus, cooling haydari, sweet-smoky muhammara and hot ezme each pair with something different, while cucumber, mint, parsley and pomegranate add fresh, tart crunch. Warm pide and sesame-crusted simit carry it all.

timeline.what: Grill the sucuk slices and warm the pide briefly.
Fill the dip bowls and drizzle olive oil over each.
Arrange the cheeses and slice the pastırma thin.
Add the olives, grape leaves, breads and produce.
Add the warm meats and scatter pomegranate seeds.

faq.q: Where can I buy sucuk and pastırma?
faq.a: Turkish, Middle Eastern and Armenian markets carry both, often spelled sujuk and basturma. Some halal butchers and online specialty shops sell them too.

faq.q: What can I use instead of beyaz peynir?
faq.a: Bulgarian white brined cheese is the closest match. A mild feta also works; soak it in cold water for 10 minutes if it's very salty.

faq.q: What do you drink with Turkish meze?
faq.a: Rakı, the anise spirit, mixed with cold water is the traditional choice. For no alcohol, serve cold ayran, a salty yogurt drink.
The dips, cheeses and grape leaves can be set out ahead. Grill the sucuk and warm the pide just before serving, since both are best warm.
